title: <project>/.homebase/known_main_failures.yml
description: Per-project allowlist of test failures that exist on main and should NOT block `homebase work finish` for branches that didn't introduce them. Demoted to a warning when the failing test matches an entry. Each entry MUST carry a tracking issue and an expiry date; expired entries hard-fail rather than silently linger. CI on main ignores the allowlist (catching new failures and discouraging cavalier additions). HMB-45 Finding 3.

check_name.description: Must match the `name` field of a required_check declared in workflow.yml (e.g. `rails_test`, `validate_docs`).

test_id.description: Substring searched for in the failing check's log output. Common forms: `Class#test_name` (Minitest), `it 'spec name'` (RSpec), `test_module.py::TestClass::test_name` (pytest). The match is literal substring (no regex) so quoting is straightforward; choose a unique anchor.

tracking_issue.description: Linear KEY-N or GitHub #N. The issue MUST exist before the entry is added; the allowlist is not a way to defer triage. Fix on main is the canonical remediation; the allowlist is a tactical bridge until the fix lands.

expires_at.description: ISO-8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD). After this date the entry hard-fails finish-time rather than demoting. Forces periodic review and prevents indefinite lingering. Set ~3 months out by default; renew explicitly if the underlying fix slips.

reason.description: One-sentence explanation of why this failure exists on main and what the fix path looks like. Read by future operators triaging an unfamiliar finish-time warning.
